overall: The AG found no violation for unanticipated end-of-meeting topics under 'Old Business' at the June 17 meeting, but found a violation for failing to timely approve the February 27 minutes without good cause.

allegations.summary: Board discussed unlisted matters at the end of its June 17 meeting under the generic 'Old Business' heading, which the complaint said was insufficient notice.
allegations.key_passage: After reviewing a recording of the June 17 meeting, we credit the Board’s account that the topics discussed at the end of the meeting were unanticipated where it appears that neither Mr. Stephens nor Ms. Flipp anticipated discussing any topics under the heading “Old Business.”

allegations.summary: Board failed to approve its February 27 open session minutes within the time allowed under the regulations, with no good cause shown.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the Board failed to timely approve the minutes of its February 27 meeting and has failed to show that it had good cause for the delay.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law's requirements.
If not already done, approve the minutes of the February 27, 2025 meeting within 30 days of the date of the letter.
remedy_passage: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the Law’s requirements and note that future similar violations may be considered evidence of an intent to violate the law. Additionally, if it has not yet done so, we order the Board to approve the minutes of its February 27, 2025, meeting within 30 days of the date of this letter.
